title: GOV: ballot-verdict/finding coherence in validate_verification_record — an APPROVE ballot citing its own OPEN MAJOR finding renders VERIFY PASS
problem:
🔎 **QA (BADF-QA)** — deferred finding from the #208 review (F-2), filed per the review-notes-become-issues rule. Out of #208's scope by construction: VER-D is ladder-internal (no gate change), and this is a `badf_gate.py` change.

## Defect
`validate_verification_record` accepts a ballot whose verdict contradicts its own cited findings. Measured probe (on `31fbc41`, #208's head, but the behavior is `main`'s — the validator is untouched by #208):

- Take `examples/verification-record-pr196-request-changes.json` (ballot cites `VF-001`, an OPEN `MAJOR` DEFECT), flip `ballots[0].verdict` `REJECT → APPROVE`, run `badf_gate.py verify` → **`BADF VERIFY PASS`**.

The #201 review's design line — "a verdict can't contradict its own findings" — is enforced at the **matrix** layer (`VERIFIED` with an OPEN blocking finding → refused, verified) but not at the **ballot** layer.

## Mitigations (why this is deferred, not urgent)
- The record "grants no verification authority" (printed on every PASS).
- A `VERIFIED` matrix row over an OPEN MAJOR is refused (VER-I15/VER-I12 family — probe confirmed).
- At dossier level, C6 refuses an OPEN MAJOR passed over / unmapped (shadow cases `open-major-passed-over`, `open-major-unmapped-pwc`).

So the incoherent ballot cannot become authority or a green dossier — but the record itself, the artifact future tooling will read, can carry a self-contradiction.

## Acceptance criteria (for the Architect to refine)
- A deterministic check in `validate_verification_record`: a PASS-class ballot verdict (`APPROVE`; `APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS` only with the finding condition-mapped, mirroring C6's mapped-vs-unmapped discrimination) may not cite a finding that is OPEN and blocking (`MAJOR`+). `REJECT` with OPEN findings stays valid (that is the honest arc).
- Failing-first: the probe above as the red test; existing five encoded records (incl. the RC record with `REJECT` + OPEN MAJOR) must still `VERIFY PASS`.
- No signature change to `validate_verification_record`; additive refusal only.

## Test list
- `test_pass_class_ballot_citing_open_blocking_finding_is_refused` (the probe, red-first)
- `test_reject_ballot_with_open_findings_still_passes` (the #196 RC record as fixture)
- `test_conditions_mapped_approve_with_conditions_passes` (the C6-mirroring discrimination)

**Version tier:** patch (additive refusal in an existing validator; ARCHI validates). **Status:** DISCOVERED (found by BADF-QA adversarial probe during the #208 review; details in #208 comment 5470744640).

note: validate_verification_record accepted a ballot whose verdict contradicted its own cited findings: APPROVE citing an OPEN MAJOR rendered VERIFY PASS. The matrix layer and check_g08_binding already refused the shape; the record's ballot layer did not. Strict APPROVE only -- APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS over an open finding is the module's own baseline fixture and the designed conditional arc, and the filed criterion to condition-map it cannot be built: the record schema carries no condition structure and no encoded record uses that verdict.
